title: Add deployment options: Docker Compose + minimal Kubernetes manifests; document resource sizing defaults
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Context
Quickstart templates currently run locally with a bare `uvicorn`/`node` process. For onboarding and supportability we need two additional deployment paths that work out-of-the-box:
1) Docker Compose dev stack (app + default vector DB) with health checks and sane resource limits
2) Minimal Kubernetes manifests suitable for “hello production” and as a starting point for Dedicated/Private clusters

Scope
- Provide Compose files for the three templates (RAG, Agents, RAG+Agents) using a consistent service name, env var contract, and health checks.
- Provide minimal K8s YAML for each template: Deployment, Service, ConfigMap (non-secret config), Secret template (not checked in with values), and Ingress notes.
- Document default resource sizing (requests/limits) and scaling knobs for:
  - API service (FastAPI / Node)
  - ingestion worker (if applicable)
  - vector DB (default backend)
- Ensure templates remain “safe by default”: no privileged containers, no hostPath mounts, no plaintext secrets in repo.

Non-goals
- Full Helm charts, production-ready multi-environment overlays, or a complete GitOps setup.
- Bundling a full observability stack (OTel collector, Prometheus, Grafana). We only document how to connect to existing infra and provide hooks.

Default backend decisions
- Compose default vector DB: Qdrant (single-node) for lowest friction.
- K8s default: also Qdrant (Deployment + PVC optional). Document how to swap adapters.

Acceptance criteria
Docker Compose
- `docker compose up` brings up:
  - app service
  - vector DB
  - (optional) ingestion worker, where template has one
- All services have `healthcheck` and Compose uses `depends_on: condition: service_healthy` where supported.
- Resource limits included (to avoid “my laptop melted” + support tickets).
- Ports are documented, and exposed ports are minimal.
- `.env.example` updated with Compose-safe defaults (localhost endpoints, no secrets committed).

Kubernetes manifests
- `kubectl apply -f k8s/` works on a vanilla cluster (kind/minikube) with minimal tweaks.
- Liveness + readiness probes included and match the template’s health endpoints.
- Resource requests/limits included and justified in docs.
- Termination grace + preStop included to support graceful shutdown.
- Clear doc section: “If deploying in Dedicated/Private, keep Redwood API key in Secret + restrict egress + enable audit logging.”

Resource sizing defaults (initial)
- App service (API):
  - requests: cpu 250m, memory 512Mi
  - limits: cpu 1, memory 1Gi
- Ingestion worker (if enabled):
  - requests: cpu 250m, memory 512Mi
  - limits: cpu 2, memory 2Gi
  - Note: ingestion memory depends on chunking + file size; docs must include guidance and failure modes.
- Qdrant:
  - requests: cpu 500m, memory 1Gi
  - limits: cpu 2, memory 4Gi
  - Storage: recommend PVC in K8s (default 10Gi) if user cares about persistence.

Notes / operational guardrails
- Make it explicit that templates call Redwood Hosted API for inference; they do not require GPUs for the app itself.
- Ensure timeouts align with SDK guidance and SRE recommendations (do not increase defaults just to mask slow ingestion).
- Document common failure modes: OOM kills during ingestion, slow startup leading to readiness failures, proxy timeouts for streaming.

Deliverables / links
- GitHub PRs expected:
  - Docker Compose: redwood-quickstarts PR (target: pr-358)
  - Kubernetes manifests: redwood-quickstarts PR (target: pr-362)
- Docs updates in repo README(s) and docs-site snippet alignment tracked separately.

Rollout
- Ship behind template minor version bump.
- Smoke tests: ensure CI brings up Compose stack and hits /health + one RAG query.

Owners / reviewers
- Owner: Bruno Silva
- Reviewers: Sean Gallagher (SRE guardrails), Marcus Lin (security defaults), Dana Lo (TS template), Monica Patel (SDK defaults for timeouts/retries)
comments: 2025-12-18 (Talia Benson): Creating this as part of the “deployment options” deliverable. Support feedback keeps pointing to “works locally but I can’t deploy it” as a drop-off point. Please keep the manifests minimal but not misleading (readiness/liveness, resource limits, graceful shutdown).

2025-12-20 (Bruno Silva): Proposal: Qdrant as the default vector DB in Compose + K8s. Postgres/pgvector is more common in prod but requires more knobs (extensions, tuning) and increases setup time. We’ll document adapter swap and keep the abstraction clean.

2025-12-23 (Sean Gallagher): +1 to resource requests/limits. Please include terminationGracePeriodSeconds and a preStop hook (sleep 5–10s) so load balancers drain. Also: don’t set super tight alerts/limits in examples—just sane container limits to prevent runaway.

2025-12-27 (Marcus Lin): Security notes: no `latest` tags, pin images; do not provide a “copy/paste secret literal” example. Include `Secret` manifest template with placeholder and point to `kubectl create secret` / sealed-secrets as options. Avoid host networking / privileged containers.

2026-01-04 (Dana Lo): For TS template, ensure Compose uses `NODE_ENV=production` for the container path and still supports local dev via `npm run dev` outside Compose. Also, the health endpoint needs to be consistent across languages (`/healthz`).

2026-01-07 (Bruno Silva): Implemented Compose stack with `app`, `qdrant`, and optional `ingest` service. Added healthchecks and set `mem_limit` in Compose. Using pinned qdrant image tag. Added docs section “Resource sizing and scaling” + notes on OOM during ingestion.

2026-01-10 (Monica Patel): Please confirm the container entrypoints respect SDK timeout defaults. We saw earlier versions set very high request timeouts “to make demos work” which then masks 429/backpressure issues. Keep defaults and document how to change them via env vars.

2026-01-14 (Bruno Silva): Added K8s manifests: Deployment/Service/ConfigMap/Secret template. Probes wired to `/healthz`. Included `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30` + preStop sleep. Documented Ingress as a note (not shipping an Ingress manifest to avoid provider-specific config).

2026-01-16 (Sean Gallagher): Reviewed YAML—looks good. One tweak: set `readinessProbe.initialDelaySeconds` a bit higher (10s) to avoid flapping on slow laptops/kind. Also ensure the worker doesn’t get a readiness probe if it’s not serving HTTP.

2026-01-18 (Marcus Lin): Approved with changes: use `redwood/quickstart-*` image names only as examples; do not imply official hosted images unless we actually publish them. Keep build instructions in README and make it clear users will build locally or via CI.

2026-01-21 (Bruno Silva): Landed via redwood-quickstarts PR-358 (Compose) and PR-362 (K8s). Added resource sizing defaults to each template README + a shared “Deployment” doc. Follow-up suggested: add CI smoke test to bring up Compose and hit `/healthz` + one query (tracked in ENG-2848).
